feature: Injectable/resettable cache for historical_rag.py training data
problem: _TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED permanently marks failed loads as empty list — a transient CSV read error disables historical defect context for the entire process lifetime. Module-level singletons also force tests to reach into private globals (_rag._TRAINING_CACHE = None) for reset, creating brittle coupling to implementation internals.
proposed_solution: 1) Expose reset_training_cache() public function that clears all 4 module-level globals to initial state. 2) Fix permanent-disable: on CSV load exception, set _TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED = False (not leave True) so a subsequent call without reset can succeed. 3) Update the autouse test fixture to call reset_training_cache() instead of directly assigning private globals. 4) Add process-level cache scope/lifetime documentation to the module docstring.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: reset_training_cache() is a public function in historical_rag.py, importable via `from commit_investigator.hypothesis.historical_rag import reset_training_cache`. Calling it resets all four module-level singletons to initial state: _TRAINING_CACHE=None, _TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED=False, _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE={}, _PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED=set(). A subsequent _load_training_data() call re-reads from CSV (observable: patch _JIT_CSV to a tmp CSV, call reset, then _load_training_data() returns rows from that file).

AC-2: The _reset_caches autouse fixture in test_historical_rag.py calls reset_training_cache() in both setup and teardown — zero direct assignments to _rag._TRAINING_CACHE, _rag._TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED, _rag._PROJECT_DIST_CACHE, or _rag._PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED anywhere inside the fixture function body.

AC-3 (source bug fix, no reset): After a simulated CSV read failure (patch _JIT_CSV to nonexistent path), call _load_training_data() once (returns []). Without calling reset_training_cache(), patch _JIT_CSV to a valid tmp CSV with ≥1 buggy row and call _load_training_data() again — returns a non-empty list. Proves the permanent-disable bug is fixed in _load_training_data(), not masked by reset.

AC-4 (reset recovery path): After the same failure sequence as AC-3, call reset_training_cache(), patch _JIT_CSV to valid CSV, call _load_training_data() — returns non-empty list. Covers explicit reset-based recovery for tests and operators.

AC-5: Module docstring documents process-level cache scope with all four elements: (a) what is cached (_TRAINING_CACHE rows, _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE per-project counts), (b) when populated (lazy on first _load_training_data / _get_project_distribution call), (c) lifetime (process-level singleton until reset or process exit), (d) how to reset (reset_training_cache()).
AC-6: Full suite regression — all existing tests pass with zero failures (pytest exit code 0; count ≥453).
edge_cases: EC-1: reset_training_cache() called before any load — no-op, no exception, globals remain at initial state.
EC-2: reset_training_cache() called after a successful load — next _load_training_data() re-reads CSV from disk (not stale in-memory list).
EC-3: Double reset (reset called twice in a row) — idempotent, globals identical to single reset.

EC-4: _PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED cleared by reset — after _get_project_distribution records a project in _PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED (even when result is {}), reset_training_cache() clears the set so the same project_key triggers _get_commit_message again on next call.

EC-5: _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE cleared by reset — after a successful _get_project_distribution caches counts for a project, reset_training_cache() clears the dict so a second call re-invokes _get_commit_message (mock call_count increases).

EC-6: Persistent CSV failure without reset — three consecutive _load_training_data() calls with a permanently missing CSV each return [] without raising, complete in bounded time (<1s total), and a fourth call after patching to a valid CSV still succeeds (proves no infinite-loop hang and recovery remains possible).

EC-7: Interleaved training load and project distribution — populate _TRAINING_CACHE and _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE/_PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED, then single reset_training_cache() clears all four globals; no partial stale state (training reload and project dist both fresh after reset).
verification_method: pytest tests/test_historical_rag.py -v (all tests pass, including new AC-3/AC-4/EC tests). pytest (full suite, exit 0, ≥453 passed). Python: `from commit_investigator.hypothesis.historical_rag import reset_training_cache` (no ImportError). Fixture isolation: `rg '_rag\._TRAINING_CACHE|_rag\._TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED|_rag\._PROJECT_DIST' tests/test_historical_rag.py` matches only inside non-fixture test bodies (fixture function `_reset_caches` must have zero matches); line 288-style direct _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE asserts may remain in tests but fixture must use reset_training_cache() only. Docstring: `python -c "import commit_investigator.hypothesis.historical_rag as m; d=m.__doc__ or ''; assert all(k in d.lower() for k in ['cache','process','reset'])"` or equivalent test asserting four doc elements.

changes: Split AC-3: added no-reset retry (source bug fix) vs reset path (AC-4); original AC-3 only proved reset works, not that _TRAINING_LOAD_ATTEMPTED=False-on-exception is implemented.
AC-1: added importability + observable re-read assertion.
AC-2: scoped private-global ban to fixture body only; aligned verification_method (full tests/ rg was contradicted by test_cache_stores_result_in_module_dict line 288).
AC-5 (was AC-4): made docstring requirements enumerable (four elements).
EC-4/EC-5: split _PROJECT_DIST_ATTEMPTED vs _PROJECT_DIST_CACHE retry behavior with observable subprocess mock assertions.
EC-6: addresses infinite-retry risk — persistent failure must return [] per call without hang, recovery still possible when CSV becomes valid.
EC-7: strengthens EC-5 interleave case with observable post-reset freshness.
